root.label: Ambico responds to U.S. tariffs without moving south

events.label: Ambico responds to U.S. tariffs without moving south

slots.name: effective tariff rate
slots.sentence: cutting the effective tariff rate on the company’s doors, which cost roughly $5,000 to $20,000 each, to about 10 percent

slots.name: U.S. business share
slots.sentence: Still, Mr. Shinder said, he will not move the company south.

slots.name: employee count
slots.sentence: “The 120 people that I employ here know that I’m not,” he said.

slots.name: steel aluminum tariff rate
slots.sentence: But after the United States imposed a 25 percent tariff on products made largely from steel or aluminum, Mr. Shinder made sure that the supplier sent only U.S.-made steel, cutting the effective tariff rate on the company’s doors, which cost roughly $5,000 to $20,000 each, to about 10 percent.

slots.name: founding date
slots.sentence: Ambico, started by Mr. Shinder’s father and uncle in 1955, initially only sold metal doors and frames around Ottawa before expanding into Montreal and Toronto.

slots.name: expansion date
slots.sentence: After Mr. Shinder returned in 1980 from university and theological studies in the U.S., he pushed to expand into upstate New York.

slots.name: free trade agreement date
slots.sentence: years before Canada and the United States signed their first free-trade agreement in 1989.
